contrast-enhanced ultrasonographic perfusion parameters of the pancreas were determined for the first time in healthy cats.
the perfusion pattern of healthy feline pancreas was described for the first time.
the pancreas of healthy cats showed a homogeneous contrast enhancement with a progressive decrease of echogenicity during wash-out phase.

the contrast-enhancement of the pancreas using a second-generation contrast medium in cats.
the use of contrast medium in cats and is the first to describe the pattern of contrast enhancement of the feline pancreatic body and left pancreatic lobe.
the use of ultrasound contrast agents in the diagnosis of pancreatic disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pancreas in normal cats has a typical perfusion pattern with an initial inflow of contrast agent into the capillary bed, followed by an increase of the splenic vein and portal vein.
the pancreas of healthy cats is perfused by the splenic artery and that contrast-enhanced ultrasonographic perfusion parameters are comparable to those of the spleen and liver.
the pancreas in normal cats is uniformly contrast enhanced at peak intensity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this study provides the first detailed description of contrast-enhanced ultrasonographic perfusion patterns in the pancreas of cats.
the pancreas is a vascular organ with a perfusion pattern similar to that of the liver.
the pancreas is an easily visualized structure in healthy cats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
contrast-enhanced ultrasonographic perfusion parameters can be obtained for the pancreas of clinically healthy cats.
contrast-enhanced ultrasonographic imaging of the pancreas may be a useful diagnostic tool to characterise pancreatic parenchymal disorders in cats.
